types.EditOp: { op: 'add'; feature: Record<string, unknown>; index?: number }
types.FaceRule: { dir?: string; normal?: Vec; planar?: boolean; at?: Vec; kind?: SurfaceKind | 'planar'; radius?: number; createdBy?: FeatureRefLike; of?: FeatureRefLike; areaGreater?: number; areaLess?: number; near?: Vec; within?: number; not?: FaceSel | FacesSel; union?: Array<FaceSel | FacesSel>; intersect?: Array<FaceSel | FacesSel>; difference?: Array<FaceSel | FacesSel>; }
types.EdgeRule: { parallel?: 'X' | 'Y' | 'Z'; outside?: [Vec, Vec]; inside?: [Vec, Vec]; not?: EdgeSel; onFace?: FaceSel | FacesSel; createdBy?: FeatureRefLike; lengthGreater?: number; lengthLess?: number; near?: Vec; within?: number; union?: EdgeSel[]; intersect?: EdgeSel[]; difference?: EdgeSel[]; }

methods.signature: at(base: PlaneBase, offset: Num = 0, opts: PlaneOpts = {}): OffsetPlane
methods.summary: A workplane for a sketch: an offset plane, a face, a plane feature, a point and normal, or a tilt.
methods.description: at(base, offset, opts) returns a plane reference for sketch(). base is 'front' (moves along +Z), 'top' (+Y), 'right' (+X); a face(...) (the plane of that planar face, offset along its outward normal); a plane feature handle from part.workplane(...) + part.handle(); or { origin: [x,y,z], normal: [x,y,z], xdir? } for any plane (axis-aligned normals use a standard plane, others add three helper points and a three-point plane). opts.rotate = { axis: 'x'|'y'|'z' | edges(...), angle } tilts the plane about that line (the plane passes through the axis; an offset is applied before the rotation). A reference plane feature is added to the part.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: 'front' | 'top' | 'right', face(sel), a plane feature handle, { origin, normal, xdir? }, or { between: [a, b] } (the mid plane of two planes or faces)

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: distance along the plane normal in mm (a number or expr), default 0

methods.notes:
- front moves along +Z, top along +Y, right along +X; a face offset goes along the face's OUTWARD normal (negative = into the body).
- { origin, normal } with a normal along a world axis is an ordinary offset plane; any other normal adds helper points and a three-point plane (7 features at most): fine for one-off tilted sketches, prefer rotate: { axis: 'x', angle } for a tilt about an axis.
- rotate turns the plane about the axis LINE, the plane passes through it; only world axes through the origin and straight edges are accepted.

methods.signature: .sketch(plane: Plane | OffsetPlane | FaceSel, build: (s: SketchBuilder) => void, name?: string): this
methods.summary: Start a sketch on a plane or a face; the next extrude, cut or revolve uses it.
methods.description: Opens a sketch on 'front' (XY, normal +Z), 'top' (XZ, normal +Y), 'right' (ZY, normal +X), on at('front', 20) (a plane moved along its normal), or on a face(): face('>Z'). The callback draws with the sketch builder `s`. A feature needs its own sketch: each extrude / cut / revolve consumes the last sketch. Units mm, Y is up.

parameters.name: build
parameters.description: callback receiving the sketch builder s

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: optional name shown in the feature tree

methods.notes:
- A sketch on a face(): the sketch origin is the world origin projected on that face; coordinates are in mm.
- Feature order matters: sketch, then the feature that uses it. Two sketches in a row without a feature between them: only the last is used.
- Units mm, Y up. front = XY (normal +Z), top = XZ (normal +Y), right = ZY (normal +X).

methods.signature: .workplane(base: PlaneBase, offset: Num = 0, opts: PlaneOpts = {}): this
methods.summary: Add a reference plane (workplane) feature without a sketch.
methods.description: workplane(base, offset, opts) adds the plane that at() would add, as a feature of its own (visible in the tree, reusable): base is 'front' | 'top' | 'right', face(...), a plane handle, or { origin, normal, xdir? }; opts.rotate tilts it about an axis line. Take part.handle() right after it, then sketch(at(handle), ...) any number of times; at(handle, 5) offsets it further.

parameters.name: base
parameters.description: 'front' | 'top' | 'right', face(sel), a plane handle or { origin, normal, xdir? }

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: distance along the normal in mm, default 0

methods.summary: The frame of a standard sketch plane: which world axes its sketch x, y and normal are.
methods.description: plane(name) returns { origin, x, y, normal, toWorld }. front: sketch x = world X, y = world Y, normal +Z. top: x = X, y = -Z (sketch y points to world -Z, so +sketch y is towards the back), normal +Y. right: x = -Z, y = Y, normal +X. Y is up. These come from the kernel's sketch frames; use toWorld([u, v], offset) to place a sketch point in the world, e.g. to aim a face selector or an expectBBox.
methods.notes: - Frames from the kernel: front x=X y=Y normal=+Z; top x=X y=-Z normal=+Y; right x=-Z y=Y normal=+X. So on 'top', sketch y grows towards world -Z; on 'right', sketch x grows towards world -Z.

methods.signature: s.arc(centre: Pt, start: Pt, end: Pt): this
methods.summary: Counter-clockwise arc about a centre from a start point to an end point.
methods.description: Adds an arc on the circle through `start` centred on `centre`, running counter-clockwise to `end` (projected on the radius). For an arc through three points in either direction use arc3.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: [x, y] where it ends (counter-clockwise from start)

methods.signature: s.arc3(a: Pt, m: Pt, b: Pt): this
methods.summary: Arc from a to b passing through the middle point m (either direction).
methods.description: Adds the arc of the circle through the three points. It fails if the points are in line. Easier than arc() when you know three points on the outline.

parameters.name: m
parameters.description: a point on the arc between a and b

methods.summary: Construction line along the sketch Y axis (the default revolve axis).
methods.description: revolve() adds this automatically when the sketch has no axis, so you rarely call it. Profile x is the distance from the axis, profile y the height along it.

methods.summary: Construction line used as the revolve axis when it is not the sketch Y axis.
methods.description: Adds a construction line between two sketch points and makes it the axis of the next revolve. Normally you pass the same thing as revolve(360, { axis: { from, to } }), which calls this for you.

methods.summary: Circle given its RADIUS (not diameter).
methods.description: Adds a circle of radius r centred on `at`. Remember radius: a 10 mm bore is circle(5). Several circles in one sketch with nesting make rings; a circle on a face with cut() makes a round pocket or a through bore.
methods.notes:
- RADIUS, not diameter: a 10 mm bore is circle(5).
- To drill, prefer part.hole / holes.* over a circle + cut: they carry the hole kind and are one feature.

methods.signature: s.grid(origin: Pt, pitch: Pt, count: [number, number]): this
methods.summary: Points on a rectangular grid.
methods.description: Adds nx by ny points starting at `origin` with spacing `pitch` along x then y (x varies fastest).

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: [nx, ny] number of points along x and y

methods.summary: One line segment between two points.
methods.description: Adds a single line from a to b. Combine with arc or arc3 to close a profile that has curved sides (a half disc is arc3 plus a line).

methods.summary: A single point (a hole centre).
methods.description: Adds a point entity. Points in a sketch are used as hole centres by hole features; for a hole use part.hole or part.holes.* rather than placing points yourself.

methods.summary: Several points (hole centres).
methods.description: Adds one point entity per [x, y]. See holes.points for the usual way to drill them.

methods.signature: s.polarPoints(center: Pt, radius: number, n: number, startAngle: number = 0): this
methods.summary: Points on a circle: a bolt circle of centres.
methods.description: Adds `n` points on a circle of `radius` about `center`, the first at `startAngle` degrees (counter-clockwise from sketch x). For drilled holes use part.holes.polar.

methods.summary: Closed polygon through the points.
methods.description: Adds a closed profile of straight lines through the points, in order; the last point joins the first. Coordinates are in the sketch plane in mm. Use it for L, T, U shapes and for revolve profiles (half cross-section).

parameters.name: pts
parameters.description: list of [x, y] points, at least three

methods.notes:
- Points go in order around the profile, either direction; the shape closes itself.
- For a revolve profile keep every x >= 0 (radius).

methods.summary: Open chain of lines through the points.
methods.description: Adds line segments joining consecutive points without closing. An open chain extrudes only when thin walls are requested (thin option) or when it is closed by other entities of the same sketch.

methods.signature: s.rect(w: Num, h: Num, at: Pt = [0, 0]): this
methods.summary: Rectangle of width x height centred on a point.
methods.description: Adds a closed rectangle: width along sketch x, height along sketch y, centred on `at` (default the sketch origin). A second rect inside the first makes a frame (ring) that extrudes as a hollow section.

methods.signature: s.rrect(w: Num, h: Num, r: Num, at: Pt = [0, 0]): this
methods.summary: Rounded rectangle: width x height with corner radius r.
methods.description: Adds four lines and four arcs that share end points, centred on `at`. With r <= 0 it is a plain rect. Prefer this over filleting the vertical edges of a plate afterwards: it is faster and more robust.

methods.signature: .chamfer(on: EdgeSel, distance: Num | { distance: Num; distance2?: Num; angle?: Num; flip?: boolean }): this
methods.summary: Bevel edges: equal distance, two distances, or distance and angle.
methods.description: Cuts a flat bevel on the chosen edges. A number is the equal distance on both faces. An options object: { distance, distance2 } measures distance on one face and distance2 on the other (chamferType distanceDistance); { distance, angle } a distance and an angle in degrees (angleDistance); flip swaps the two faces. NOTE: the current kernel implements only the equal-distance chamfer: the two-distance and angle forms are emitted as the kernel's features but fail with an `unsupported` error until the kernel adds them; model those bevels with a cut or a sketch polygon instead. Good for edge breaks on bores and rims.

parameters.name: distance
parameters.type: Num | { distance: Num; distance2?: Num; angle?: Num; flip?: boolean }
parameters.description: mm (number or expr), or { distance, distance2?, angle?, flip? }

methods.notes: - Only the equal-distance chamfer is implemented by the kernel today. { distance, distance2 } and { distance, angle } are emitted but come back as an `unsupported` error: cut the bevel with a sketch polygon instead.

methods.summary: Cut the last sketch out of the body: a depth or through().
methods.description: Removes material. direction: 'into' (the kernel default: AGAINST the sketch normal, which is into the body from a face sketch), 'away' (along the normal), 'both' (symmetric about the sketch plane; depth is the total) or 'auto' (the default for cuts: try 'into'; if the kernel reports cutNoEffect because the body is on the other side, flip once and add the warning 'cut direction flipped automatically'). Give direction explicitly to avoid the extra build. Depth is a number or through() for all the way. Same other options as extrude (mid, flip, draft, thin).

properties.name: direction
properties.description: 'auto' (default: into, flip once if nothing is cut) | 'into' | 'away' | 'both'

methods.notes:
- Direction is relative to the SKETCH NORMAL: 'into' = against it (the kernel's default for a cut, into the body from a face sketch), 'away' = along it, 'both' = symmetric about the sketch plane (depth is the total). The default is 'auto': try 'into'; if the kernel says cutNoEffect, flip once and add the warning 'cut direction flipped automatically'. Pass the direction yourself to skip the retry.
- front/top/right normals are +Z/+Y/+X: a cut sketched on 'front' at z = 0 with the body above it (z > 0) is 'away'.
- A cut sketch must overlap the material in plan; a circle outside the body gives `cutNoEffect` in BOTH directions (the auto flip does not hide it).
- Several shapes in ONE sketch are ONE cut feature (draw pockets in a loop, then cut once).
- Depth beyond the body is fine; through() is clearer when you mean all the way.

methods.summary: Extrude the last sketch into a solid (adds material).
methods.description: Extrudes the last sketch along its plane normal by `depth` mm. Options: direction ('away' = along the sketch normal, the default; 'into' = against it; 'both' = symmetric about the plane, depth is the total, same as mid), flip (the old way to reverse), draft (taper angle in degrees), thin (hollow wall thickness: closed profile gives a tube, open profile a thin sheet). Sketch normals: front +Z, top +Y, right +X (see plane()); a face sketch's normal points out of the body. The first extrude makes the body; later ones add to it (a boss when sketched on a face).

properties.name: mid
properties.description: extrude half each way (same as direction: 'both'; symmetric: true is the same)

properties.name: thin
properties.description: wall thickness for a thin-walled extrude

properties.name: direction
properties.description: 'away' (along the sketch normal, default) | 'into' (against it) | 'both' (symmetric, depth is the total)

methods.notes:
- Each extrude consumes the sketch before it: sketch again for the next feature.
- A sketch on a face adds material outward (a boss). On the 'front' plane it goes +Z, on 'top' +Y, on 'right' +X; direction 'into' reverses, 'both' (or mid) is symmetric with depth as the total.
- On the 'top' and 'right' planes the sketch axes are not x/y of the world (top: sketch y = world -Z; right: sketch x = world -Z); see plane() for the table.
- Nested closed shapes in one sketch (rect inside rect) give a ring, not two solids.
- draft is in degrees and tapers the sides inward for a positive angle on a boss.

methods.signature: .fillet(on: EdgeSel, radius: Num | { radius?: Num | Num[] | Record<string, Num>; variable?: [Num, Num] }): this
methods.summary: Round edges: one radius, a radius per edge, or a variable radius.
methods.description: Rounds the edges chosen by edges(). radius is a number (constant), or an options object: { radius: number | number[] | {[edgeKey]: number} } where an array gives one radius per selected edge in selection order (its length must equal the edge count) and an object maps edge keys (like 'F2.C0|F2.S.l1#0', as listed by part.edges... or '*' for the rest) to radii; edges with different radii become one fillet feature per distinct radius, applied in order of increasing radius (so a sequence of fillets, not one simultaneous blend: edges that meet at a vertex can fail with blendOverflow, then give them the same radius). { variable: [near, far] } makes ONE fillet whose radius changes linearly along each selected edge from the end nearer the start to the far end. Fails when a radius is too big for the adjacent faces (blendOverflow). Fillet before shelling and before adding small features; select with edges('|Z') for the vertical edges of a block.

parameters.name: radius
parameters.type: Num | { radius?: Num | Num[] | Record<string, Num>; variable?: [Num, Num] }
parameters.description: radius in mm (number or expr), or { radius, variable }

methods.notes:
- A radius that is too big for the neighbouring faces gives `blendOverflow`: halve it. Radius equal to half a face width is already a limit.
- Fillet before shell and before small holes; fillet edges('|Z') for the vertical edges of a block, or draw sketch.rrect instead.
- A fillet selected by edges() of faces that do not exist yet fails with a Line N selector error: select at the point in the chain where the edge exists.
- Different radii on edges that meet at a corner are applied as SEQUENTIAL fillets (one per distinct radius, increasing) and can fail with blendFailed where a simultaneous blend would not; use one radius there, or fillet the corners in a sketch (rrect).
- { variable: [near, far] } works on isolated edges; edge junctions (all four edges of a face) fail with blendFailed.

methods.signature: .revolve(angle: Num = 360, o: { op?: 'add' | 'cut'; thin?: Num; axis?: { from: Pt; to: Pt } } = {}): this
methods.summary: Revolve the last sketch about an axis (lathe parts: pulleys, bushings, flanges).
methods.description: Revolves the last sketch `angle` degrees (default 360). The axis is the sketch Y axis unless axis: { from, to } gives a line in the sketch plane. Profile x is the radius, y the height along the axis, so draw a half cross-section on one side of the axis. op: 'cut' removes the revolved volume instead. thin makes a revolved shell.

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { op?: 'add' | 'cut'; thin?: Num; axis?: { from: Pt; to: Pt } }

properties.name: thin
properties.description: wall thickness for a thin revolve

properties.name: axis
properties.description: { from: [x, y], to: [x, y] } axis line in the sketch plane

methods.notes:
- Draw the half profile on ONE side of the axis: x is the distance from the axis, y the height. Keep the profile from crossing the axis (no negative x).
- The sketch plane decides the world axis: on 'front' and 'right' the sketch Y axis is world Y or world Z accordingly; for a pulley on 'right' the axis is world Y and the end faces are face('>Y') / face('<Y').
- 360 is a full solid of revolution; a smaller angle leaves two planar end faces.

methods.summary: Hollow the body to a wall thickness, opening the selected face(s).
methods.description: Hollows out the solid leaving walls of `thickness` mm and removing the selected face to make an opening (box open at the top: shell(face('>Z'), 2)). faces(...) opens several faces at once. Do fillets of the outside edges before the shell. A thickness larger than the smallest feature fails (shellTooThick).

parameters.name: open
parameters.description: face(sel) or faces(sel) of the face(s) left open

methods.notes:
- Fillet or chamfer the OUTSIDE edges before shelling; shelling a rounded box keeps even walls.
- The selected face is REMOVED (the opening). To close the box again sketch a lid on the rim face and extrude it (recipe hollow-box-lid).
- A thickness that is too big gives shellTooThick / shellFailed with maxThickness in the error.

methods.summary: Make the previous extrude or revolve a thin-walled one.
methods.description: Edits the step recorded just before it: the same as passing the thin option. Closed profile gives a hollow section of this wall thickness (centred on the profile).

methods.summary: End condition for cut(): through all material.
methods.description: through() is passed to cut() instead of a depth to cut all the way through the body, in the direction the cut goes (against the sketch normal).

methods.summary: Select edges of the current body by direction, extreme plane, or a rule object.
methods.description: edges(sel) is resolved against the body just before the step that uses it. Strings: 'all'; '|X' '|Y' '|Z' straight edges parallel to that axis; '>X' ... '<Z' edges lying in the extreme plane along that axis. A rule object ANDs its keys: parallel ('X'|'Y'|'Z'), outside / inside (box [[x0,y0,z0],[x1,y1,z1]] tested on the edge midpoint), not (another edges()), onFace (a face() or faces()), createdBy (edges that bound a face a feature created: a handle or id), lengthGreater, lengthLess, near + within (radius), and union / intersect / difference (arrays of edges()). It fails with a line number when nothing matches.

parameters.name: sel
parameters.description: a selector string, or an EdgeRule object

methods.notes:
- Rule keys AND together; use union / intersect / difference for combinations.
- edges('>Z') selects edges lying in the highest plane only (after a boss, that is the boss rim). Combine with onFace or not to refine.
- A selector that matches nothing is an error with the script line, not a silent no-op.

methods.signature: face(sel: string | FaceRule, opts: { of?: FeatureRefLike } = {}): FaceSel
methods.summary: Select ONE face of the current body: by direction, by persistent name, by feature, or by a rule.
methods.description: face(sel, opts) is resolved when the script runs, against the body as it is just before the step that uses it. A direction '>X' '<X' '>Y' '<Y' '>Z' '<Z' ('#top' '#bottom') is the planar face whose outward normal is that axis and which lies furthest along it (ties: the biggest). AFTER A BOSS OR POCKET '>Z' means the boss top, and the plate top facing the same way is a different face: when other faces face the same way but belong to another feature, the run result carries a warning naming the face it resolved to; pick on purpose with face('>Z', { of: handle }) (only faces created by that feature: a handle from part.handle(), or an id like 'F2'). A persistent face name such as 'F3.C1' (cap 1 of F3) selects exactly that face; 'F3.*' is a prefix. A rule object ANDs its keys: dir, normal [x,y,z] (planar faces facing that way), planar, at [x,y,z] (planar: the point lies on its plane), kind ('plane'|'cylinder'|'sphere'|'other'), radius, createdBy / of (feature), areaGreater, areaLess, near [x,y,z] (+ within), not / union / intersect / difference (arrays of face() or faces()). It must match exactly one face (faces(rule).nth(i), .largest(), .smallest(), .near(p) choose among several); it fails with a line number otherwise. Pass it to sketch(), at(), hole(), holes.*, shell().

parameters.name: sel
parameters.description: '>X' '<X' '>Y' '<Y' '>Z' '<Z' '#top' '#bottom', a face name ('F3.C1'), or a FaceRule object

parameters.name: opts
parameters.description: { of: feature handle or id } restrict to the faces that feature created

methods.example:
part('Plate').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(60, 40)).extrude(10)
  .sketch(face('>Z'), (s) => s.circle(12)).extrude(15)
  .hole(face('>Z'), [0, 0], { diameter: 8 })
  .hole(face('>Z', { of: 'F2' }), [25, 0], { diameter: 5 });
methods.notes:
- A direction ('>Z') matches planar faces by outward normal, the furthest first, ties to the biggest. After a boss or a pocket several faces face the same way: the run result then carries a WARNING naming the face it resolved to and the others. Read warnings; choose on purpose with face('>Z', { of: handle }) (handle = part.handle() right after the feature) or a face name.
- Persistent names ('F3.C1' = cap 1 of F3, 'F3.S.e2' = side of sketch entity e2, 'F8.C0@F10.1' = pattern copy) survive edits that keep the feature; list them with `await part.faces()`.
- A rule object must match exactly ONE face; for several use faces(rule) and .nth(i) / .largest() / .smallest() / .near([x,y,z]).
- Resolved against the body as it is just before the step: after a boss on top, face('>Z') is the boss top, not the plate top.

methods.signature: faces(sel: string | FaceRule, opts: { of?: FeatureRefLike } = {}): FacesSel
methods.summary: Select SEVERAL faces (a set) of the current body, or choose one of them by order, size or position.
methods.description: faces(sel, opts) takes the same specs as face() but returns every match: faces({ kind: 'cylinder', radius: 5 }) is every R5 cylindrical face, faces({ createdBy: h }) every face a feature created, faces('>Z') every face facing +Z. Use it where several faces are wanted (shell(faces(...), t) opens them all, edges({ onFace: faces(...) })), or chain one pick: .nth(i) (position in the body's face list), .largest(), .smallest(), .first(), .last(), .near([x, y, z]) (centroid nearest the point); each returns a face() you can pass to sketch() or hole().

parameters.name: sel
parameters.description: a direction, a face name or prefix ('F3.*'), or a FaceRule (see face)

parameters.name: opts
parameters.description: { of: feature handle or id } restrict to the faces that feature created

methods.example:
part('Block').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 30)).extrude(20)
  .sketch(face('>Z'), (s) => s.circle(6)).cut(through())
  .fillet(edges({ onFace: faces({ kind: 'cylinder', radius: 6 }) }), 1)
  .shell(faces('<Z').largest(), 2);
methods.notes:
- .nth(i) counts in the body's face list order (stable for one script, not geometric). Prefer .largest(), .smallest(), .near(point) or a rule that pins the face.
- kind and radius come from the display mesh (radius within 0.2 percent); cone and torus faces are kind 'other' for selection (part.faces() read-back reports the kernel's exact surface type).
- shell(faces(...), t) opens several faces at once; edges({ onFace: faces(...) }) takes the edges of any of them.

methods.signature: .hole(on: FaceSel, at: Pt, o: { diameter: Num; depth?: Num; flip?: boolean }): this
methods.summary: A simple drilled hole on a planar face at [x, y].
methods.description: Drills a round hole into the material from the face. [x, y] are coordinates in the sketch plane of that face, measured from the part origin projected onto it (not from a corner). Through unless depth is given. Use flip: true if it cuts the wrong way on an unusual face. Diameter, not radius.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: face(sel) of the planar face to drill from

parameters.name: at
parameters.description: [x, y] hole centre in the face sketch plane

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { diameter: Num; depth?: Num; flip?: boolean }

properties.name: depth
properties.description: blind depth in mm, omit for through

methods.notes:
- diameter, not radius (circle() is radius). Centres are in the face sketch plane relative to the world origin projected on the face, NOT a corner of the face: a hole at [0, 0] on a plate centred on the origin is in the middle.
- face('>Z') must exist as a planar face at that step. After a shell or fillet on the top, the top face may be a different face: select again.
- Through unless depth is given. Many holes: use holes.points / polar / grid (one feature).

methods.signature: .holes.grid(on: FaceSel, g: { origin: Pt; pitch: Pt; count: [number, number] }, o: { diameter: Num; depth?: Num; flip?: boolean }): this
methods.summary: A rectangular grid of holes.
methods.description: Drills nx by ny holes from `origin` at `pitch` spacing, as one feature.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: face(sel) of the face to drill from

parameters.name: g
parameters.type: { origin: Pt; pitch: Pt; count: [number, number] }
parameters.description: { origin: [x, y], pitch: [dx, dy], count: [nx, ny] }

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { diameter: Num; depth?: Num; flip?: boolean }

methods.example:
part('Perf').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(60, 40)).extrude(4)
  .holes.grid(face('>Z'), { origin: [-20, -10], pitch: [10, 10], count: [5, 3] }, { diameter: 4 });

methods.signature: .holes.points(on: FaceSel, pts: Pt[], o: { diameter: Num; depth?: Num; flip?: boolean }): this
methods.summary: Drill holes at listed coordinates: one hole feature at a list of centres.
methods.description: All holes share diameter and depth. Centres are [x, y] coordinates in the face sketch plane.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: face(sel) of the face to drill from

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { diameter: Num; depth?: Num; flip?: boolean }

methods.signature: .holes.polar(on: FaceSel, c: { center: Pt; radius: number; count: number; startAngle?: number }, o: { diameter: Num; depth?: Num; flip?: boolean }): this
methods.summary: A bolt circle: count holes equally spaced on a circle.
methods.description: Drills `count` holes on a circle of `radius` about `center` (sketch-plane coordinates, usually [0, 0]), the first at startAngle degrees. All holes are one feature.

parameters.name: on
parameters.description: face(sel) of the face to drill from

parameters.name: c
parameters.type: { center: Pt; radius: number; count: number; startAngle?: number }
parameters.description: { center: [x, y], radius, count, startAngle? degrees }

parameters.name: o
parameters.type: { diameter: Num; depth?: Num; flip?: boolean }

methods.example:
part('Flange plate').sketch('front', (s) => s.circle(40)).extrude(8)
  .holes.polar(face('>Z'), { center: [0, 0], radius: 28, count: 6 }, { diameter: 6 });
methods.notes:
- One feature for the whole bolt circle. center is [x, y] in the face sketch plane (usually [0, 0] for a centred disc); startAngle shifts the first hole (degrees).
- Check that radius + diameter/2 stays inside the face and that holes do not overlap the centre bore.

methods.summary: Repeat features around an axis.
methods.description: circularPattern(o) repeats the feature added just before it; circularPattern(seed, o) repeats seed ('last', a handle, a feature id, or an array). Instances: count in total over angle (alias total) degrees, 360 = a full circle. axis is 'x' | 'y' | 'z', [ox, oy, oz, dx, dy, dz] or a straight edge; the kernel rotates about a WORLD axis through the origin only, so an offset or oblique axis fails with a clear error (centre the part on the axis, or use holes.polar for a bolt circle anywhere). equalSpacing (default true for 360) spaces the instances angle / count apart; false spaces them angle / (count - 1) so the last lands exactly at the end angle (use it for an arc fan). A pattern can seed another pattern.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: 'last', a handle, a feature id or an array of them (omit to repeat the last feature)

properties.name: angle
properties.description: total angle in degrees, default 360 (alias total)

properties.name: equalSpacing
properties.description: angle / count apart (default when 360); false: angle / (count - 1)

methods.notes:
- The axis is a WORLD axis through the origin (x, y, z, [0,0,0,dx,dy,dz] or a straight edge lying on one); an offset axis is refused with a Line N error. Centre the part on it, or use holes.polar for a bolt circle at any centre.
- equalSpacing (default for 360) steps angle / count; set it false with a partial angle to put the last copy exactly at the end angle.
- Several features: pass an array of handles as the first argument.

methods.summary: Repeat features along a direction, optionally as a 2D grid.
methods.description: linearPattern(o) repeats the feature added just before it; linearPattern(seed, o) repeats seed: 'last', a handle from part.handle(), a feature id like 'F4', or an array of those (several features are patterned together). Instances: count in total (including the original), every spacing mm, or totalLength mm from first to last (spacing = totalLength / (count - 1)). direction (or axis) is 'x' | 'y' | 'z', a vector [x, y, z] or a straight edge: the kernel patterns along the WORLD axes only, so a vector or edge must be parallel to x, y or z (its sign picks the way); anything oblique fails with a clear error. reverse flips the way. second: { direction, count, spacing | totalLength } adds a second direction: the original features plus the first pattern are patterned again (a pattern of a pattern, which the kernel supports) giving count x second.count instances, a rectangular grid.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description: 'last', a handle, a feature id or an array of them (omit to repeat the last feature)

properties.name: totalLength
properties.description: first-to-last distance in mm instead of spacing

properties.name: second
properties.type: { direction?: 'x' | 'y' | 'z' | Vec | EdgeSel; axis?: 'x' | 'y' | 'z'; count: number; spacing?: Num; totalLength?: Num; reverse?: boolean }
properties.description: { direction, count, spacing | totalLength, reverse? } the second grid direction

methods.notes:
- count includes the original; spacing is between instances in mm (or totalLength from first to last).
- The kernel patterns along WORLD x, y or z only: a vector or an edge must be parallel to an axis. Oblique directions are refused with a Line N error.
- Several features: pass an array of handles ([a, b]) as the first argument. A 2D grid is `second: { direction, count, spacing }`.
- A pattern can seed another pattern; the grid helper seeds the second pattern with the originals plus the first pattern (a pattern alone omits its own original).
- Prefer holes.grid when the repeated thing is only drilled holes.

methods.summary: A parameter written as an expression over the variables.
methods.description: expr('w/2') keeps the feature parameter linked to the variable w (stored as =w/2). Inside a sketch an expr contributes its current number only. Characters are limited to arithmetic and Math.*.
methods.example:
const { w } = variables({ w: 40 });
part('Bar').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(w, 10)).extrude(expr('w/4'));

methods.summary: Start the part the script builds; returns the fluent builder.
methods.description: Every script builds one part (the last wins). Chain sketch, extrude, cut, holes, fillet, ... on the result. The name appears as the document name.

methods.summary: Read the total surface area (mm2) of the part built so far.
methods.description: Like volume(): forces a build of what is recorded so far and a mass-properties query, cached until the next feature. Needs await.
methods.example:
const p = part('Cube').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(10, 10)).extrude(10);
const a = await p.area();   // 600

methods.signature: .bbox(): Promise<{ min: Vec; max: Vec; size: Vec }>
methods.summary: Read the bounding box of the part built so far.
methods.description: Returns { min: [x, y, z], max: [x, y, z], size: [dx, dy, dz] } in mm. Forces a view build of what is recorded so far (the display body carries the box); cached until the next feature. Needs await.
methods.returns: Promise<{ min: Vec; max: Vec; size: Vec }>
methods.example:
const p = part('Block').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 30)).extrude(20);
const b = await p.bbox();   // size [40, 30, 20], min [-20, -15, 0]

methods.summary: Read the centre of mass of the part built so far.
methods.description: Returns [x, y, z] in mm (uniform density). Forces a build and a mass-properties query, cached until the next feature. Needs await.
methods.example:
const p = part('Block').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 30)).extrude(20);
const c = await p.centreOfMass();   // [0, 0, 10]

methods.summary: Read the number of edges of the part built so far.
methods.description: Counts the edges of the display body (seam-split arcs count once); cached until the next feature. Needs await.
methods.example:
const p = part('Block').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 30)).extrude(20);
const n = await p.edgeCount();   // 12

methods.signature: .edges(): Promise<Array<{ key: string; mid: Vec; length: number; faces: string[] }>>
methods.summary: Read the edges of the part built so far: key, midpoint, length, adjacent faces.
methods.description: Returns { key, mid, length, faces } per edge. The key (like 'F2.C0|F2.S.l1#0') is what the object form of fillet({ radius: { [key]: r } }) takes. Needs await.
methods.returns: Promise<Array<{ key: string; mid: Vec; length: number; faces: string[] }>>
methods.example:
const p = part('Block').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 30)).extrude(20);
const es = await p.edges();   // 12 edges

methods.signature: .expectBBox(box: { min?: Vec; max?: Vec; size?: Vec }, o: { tol?: number } = {}): this
methods.summary: Check the bounding box of the part built so far.
methods.description: expectBBox({ min, max, size }, { tol }) checks the keys you give (each [x, y, z]) to an absolute tol in mm (default 1e-3). Use size to check the extents without caring where the part sits. No await needed.

parameters.name: box
parameters.type: { min?: Vec; max?: Vec; size?: Vec }
parameters.description: { min?, max?, size? } each [x, y, z]

methods.summary: Check the number of faces of the part built so far.
methods.description: expectFaceCount(n) fails with the actual count when it differs. A cheap regression check after patterns and fillets. No await needed.

methods.summary: Check that the part built so far passes the kernel's validity check.
methods.description: expectValid() fails with the validator's first issue (code and entity) as an error with this line. No await needed.

methods.signature: .expectVolume(v: number, o: { tol?: number; abs?: number } = {}): this
methods.summary: Check the volume of the part built so far; a mismatch is reported as an error with this line.
methods.description: expectVolume(v, { tol }) compares with relative tolerance tol (default 1e-3), or { abs } in mm3. No await needed: it is a step, checked when the runner reaches it (a build of what is recorded so far, cached with other reads). A failure is listed in the run errors as 'Line N: expected volume V, got W' and the run goes on. The volume is the kernel's exact value, so analytic references (boxes, cylinders) match to 1e-6.

properties.name: abs
properties.description: absolute tolerance in mm3 (instead of tol)

methods.notes: - tol is relative (default 1e-3); pass { abs } for mm3. A failed expectation is an error with its line; the run goes on, but an agent run with errors does not replace the document.

methods.summary: Read the number of faces of the part built so far.
methods.description: Counts the faces of the display body; cached until the next feature. Needs await.
methods.example:
const p = part('Block').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 30)).extrude(20);
const n = await p.faceCount();   // 6

methods.summary: Read the faces of the part built so far: persistent name, kind, area, normal, centre, radius, feature.
methods.description: Returns a list of { name, kind ('plane' | 'cylinder' | 'sphere' | 'other'), area, normal (planar faces), center, radius (round faces), feature }. The name works in face('F3.C1'). Use it to find the face you mean before selecting it; the surface kind and radius are fitted from the display mesh. Forces a view build of what is recorded so far, cached until the next feature. Needs await.
methods.example:
const p = part('Plate').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(60, 40)).extrude(10).hole(face('>Z'), [0, 0], { diameter: 8 });
const bores = (await p.faces()).filter((f) => f.kind === 'cylinder');   // one R4 bore

methods.summary: A handle on the feature recorded last, for face({ of }) and patterns.
methods.description: handle() returns an object naming the feature the previous call added (its id is filled in when the script runs): const boss = part.handle() after .extrude(15). Then face('>Z', { of: boss }) selects only the faces that feature created, faces({ createdBy: boss }) all of them, edges({ createdBy: boss }) their edges, and linearPattern(boss, ...) repeats it. After a sketch it names the sketch; after a hole() the hole feature (a hole's sketch is internal). Placing a handle costs nothing.
methods.notes: - Take the handle right AFTER the feature it names. A handle used before it is resolved gives a Line N error. The handle names a hole() feature, not the internal sketch of it.

methods.signature: .issues(): Promise<Array<{ code: string; entity: string; detail: string }>>
methods.summary: Read the validator's issues for the part built so far.
methods.description: Returns a list of { code, entity, detail }, empty when the part is valid. Needs await.
methods.returns: Promise<Array<{ code: string; entity: string; detail: string }>>
methods.example:
const p = part('Block').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 30)).extrude(20);
const issues = await p.issues();   // []

methods.summary: Read whether the part built so far passes the kernel's validity check.
methods.description: true when the validator finds no issue; the issues come from part.issues(). Forces a build and a validate query, cached until the next feature. Needs await.
methods.example:
const p = part('Block').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(40, 30)).extrude(20);
const ok = await p.isValid();   // true

methods.summary: Read the volume (mm3) of the part built so far.
methods.description: await part.volume() makes the runner build everything recorded up to here on the scratch kernel (a full regeneration of the features so far, then a mass-properties query), returns the number and the script continues recording. Use it to compute the next dimension from a real result or to print a check. The script must use await (top level await is allowed). COST: every read forces an intermediate build; the answer is cached until the next feature is added, so read once, after a group of features, not inside a loop of features. Compare with the expect* helpers, which need no await.
methods.notes:
- Needs `await`. Every read forces an intermediate regeneration of everything recorded so far (a full build on the scratch kernel, a view build for bbox/faces/counts); the answer is cached until the next feature is added. Read once after a group of features, never inside a loop that adds features.
- Use the expect* helpers (expectVolume, expectValid, expectBBox, expectFaceCount) when you only want to assert: no await, errors carry the script line.

methods.signature: variables(defs: Record<string, number | string>): Record<string, number>
methods.summary: Declare named values; strings are expressions over earlier ones.
methods.description: variables({ w: 60, t: 'w/10' }) defines document variables (editable in the Variables tab) and returns their numbers for use in the script. Use expr('w*2') to keep a feature parameter linked to a variable instead of a fixed number.
methods.example:
const { w, t } = variables({ w: 60, t: 'w/10' });
part('Bar').sketch('front', (s) => s.rect(w, 10)).extrude(expr('t'));
